output.reason: The buffer distance of 500 has no units, and the input point is in WGS 84 (geographic degrees). A 500-degree buffer would be meaningless, so the intended unit is unknown. Please specify the unit, for example meters or kilometers. If meters are intended, a geodesic buffer or a reprojection to a suitable metric CRS (such as UTM zone 33N, EPSG:32633) would be needed, and the result can be returned in WGS 84.

The points layer states no CRS, and its coordinates (about 391390, 5817855) look like projected metres, not the degrees used by the zones (about 13.3 to 13.7 E, 52.4 to 52.6 N). The within test needs both layers in the same CRS, so the CRS of the points must be supplied before the join can run. I have not assumed one (for example EPSG:25833) because that would be a guess.
The input layer contains only the features alpha, bravo, charlie, and delta. Neither "echo" nor "foxtrot" exists in the data, so the geodesic distance between them cannot be computed.

no_points_within_zones: all six points (lon 13.35 to 13.80, lat 52.42 to 52.55, Berlin area) lie outside both Paris zones (lon 2.25 to 2.42, lat 48.80 to 48.90), so the inner within-join returns no matches and the data cannot say which Paris zone any point is in

ambiguous_projection: a planar distance in EPSG:4326 is computed in degrees, not meters. Meters need a projected CRS (for example EPSG:32633 UTM zone 33N, which covers these points), or the user could ask for a geodesic distance instead.
Inward buffer of 50 international feet (15.24 m, exact) applied to the 200 m x 100 m rectangle with mitred corners, giving a 169.52 m x 69.52 m rectangle.
spherical Web Mercator forward projection of WGS 84 (OGC:CRS84) lon/lat with R = 6378137 m

unknown_crs: target_crs "EPSG:999999" does not appear to be a defined EPSG code, so the point cannot be transformed to it. I have no tools here to query the CRS registry, so this is based on my knowledge of EPSG, not a lookup. Please supply a valid target CRS.

Transformed from OGC:CRS84 (WGS 84 lon/lat) to UTM zone 56S (central meridian 153E, k0 0.9996, false easting 500000 m, false northing 10000000 m). Computed by hand with the Krüger/TM series on the WGS 84 ellipsoid, so the values are accurate to roughly centimetres, not verified against PROJ.

Planar distance between midtown (-73.9857, 40.7484) and uptown (-73.968, 40.7851) after projecting to UTM 18N. Hand-computed, not run in code: ellipsoidal distance of about 4340.868 m times the UTM point scale factor (about 0.999692) gives about 4339.530 m, or 2.69646 statute miles (1 mi = 1609.344 m). Expect the last digit to be uncertain.
intersection of parcels with flood zones; three overlapping pairs (a1-f1, a2-f1, a3-f2); a1-f2, a2-f2 and a3-f1 do not overlap
inner_join_contains_point_attributes; points p4 (13.5, 52.5) lies on the shared boundary of z1 and z2 and is not contained by either; p5 lies outside both zones

limitations: Small synthetic fixtures; they test operation correctness, not scale or real-world data quality.
Expected outputs come from one reference workflow (Shapely, pyproj, GEOS, PROJ); an error shared by those libraries would not be caught.
Tolerances are set per case and stated in explicit units, sized to catch the smallest error of the mistake each case targets; none is tighter than a correct answer given to 5 decimal places needs.

benchmark.notes: Every expected output is computed by reference.py; regenerate them with `geoevals bench regenerate gis_correctness`.
